quest.title: The Wingless One of Tlalocan
quest.description: There seems to be a crestfallen person near the Flower-Feather Clan...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x35475, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Act I
chapter.title: The Wingless One of Tlalocan

talks.objective: Head to the area near the Flower-Feather Clan

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, why's she crying? Should we go check on her? Y'know, just in case she's... thinking of doing something stupid...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'd leave her be.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The warriors of the Flower-Feather Clan are a proud bunch, who never show their vulnerability in public... Even if they've gone wingless.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you're that fan favorite from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame! Ch... Ch...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Chasca.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'm flattered that you remember my name. Your reputations precede you too, Travelers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what are you doing here? Paimon figured you'd all be off fighting in the Night Warden Wars by now.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'll be heading there shortly. But there are some things I want to get taken care of before I go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! ...Chasca?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: #Good to see you again, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Before we carry on — let's get a little further away before Coyllur notices us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that girl on the bridge — Coyllur, you said? Should she really be on her own right now? With the mental state she's in, it just seems risky...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Don't worry, that's exactly why I'm here. Elder Allpa sent me to keep an eye on her. If she does attempt the unthinkable, I'll swoop in and catch her.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I doubt it'll come to that, though. She's a fighter — a warrior, in fact. One who aimed for the sky. However despondent she might feel now, I'm confident she'll get through it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "aimed for the sky"?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well, in the Flower-Feather Clan there's an elite flying squad made up of qucusaur riders.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But it's an extremely selective squad. To become a rider, you need to undergo a trial where you not only demonstrate mastery of the relevant skills, but also win the approval of the qucusaurs. Very few candidates make it through the process.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Coyllur has spent years training for her most recent attempt, but unfortunately she didn't pass... So it's not hard to see why she's so upset.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And when you mentioned "going wingless," what does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Sometimes, after multiple failed attempts to pass the flying test and win the qucusaurs' approval, people get so disheartened that they give up on their dream to soar the skies.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: They resolve to quit trying for good. We call those people the "Wingless."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *gasp* Do they get expelled from the tribe!?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: What? No, of course not. They're still prized warriors.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: We have a saying: "Just as the qucusaur treasures every feather on its body, so the tribe treasures each one of its children."

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: This hits even harder in the wake of the war... All of our young warriors carry the future of our tribe on their shoulders.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Besides, every qucusaur falls from its nest before it learns to fly. It's practically a rite of passage. Likewise, for the Wingless, we always hold out hope that one day when they're ready, they'll rekindle their dreams and keep trying.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Until then, all we can do is quietly watch over them from a distance... just like I'm doing now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, okay... Paimon hopes she'll get back on her feet soon!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Well, from the sound of her whistling, her confidence has been seriously shaken. No qucusaur is gonna respond to a call that sounds like that.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Yeah, people from my tribe call to their saurian companions by whistling or blowing a horn. So it sounds like Coyllur was trying to summon a qucusaur to practice her flying.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: But the qucusaurs are an even prouder bunch than our warriors... They would never respond to a lackluster whistle like that.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: First she failed the trial, and now she's struggling to even summon a qucusaur. That's only gonna hurt her confidence further... And getting trapped in that vicious circle is the kind of thing that'll make people go wingless.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Surely, there must be something we can do to help?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: That's very kind of you. Coyllur's flying skills are up to par, but mentally, she's stuck in a rut. If she wants to return to the sky, she has to overcome that for herself.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I'm going to lay low nearby, just in case she takes a turn for the worse. Let me give you a tour around the tribe once this is all over.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Coyllur still isn't giving up! Even though Chasca said that she has to do this by herself, Paimon can't help feeling like maybe we can nudge her in the right direction...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... What if we could get a qucusaur to fly up to her? That might give her the confidence boost she needs.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Actually, that sounds like a plan...)

talks.objective: Indwell a Qucusaurus to get close to Coyllur
Perform an indwelling and then talk to Coyllur

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: It's... It's a qu-qucusaur! Oh my gosh, is this really happening? I did it, I summoned one!

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: I was beginning to think you'd all given up on me completely... Thank you! Oh, thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like her mood's lifted. Now to wait till she's not looking, and fly outta here...)

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Excuse me... would you mind if we did some flying practice together right now?

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: I think I know where I went wrong in the test now — I need to maintain a higher speed on my turns! So I just gotta practice my Bell Tailslides and Split S maneuvers...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Yikes, those sound complicated... I'm out of my depth. This is too dangerous.)

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: ...Also, I really wanna try some stall turns and cobra maneuvers...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Crikey. I've never even carried a passenger, let alone while doing all that... I need to get out of here!)

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Huh? That sounded like a whistle... Is someone else trying to summon a qucusaur?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Now's my chance!)

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Hey! Wait! Wait...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With the whistle providing the perfect cover, you make your escape...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: #Hmm... A golden-haired outlander, and a white flying object... You must be {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: I heard Chasca was with you, but I suppose she's run away again, has she...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... sorry, who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: Who am I? Tsk, only her father!

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: She's supposed to go for a checkup every three months to see how her Abyss condition is doing. We both agreed on it... But she's already missed three checkups this year! That's three out of four!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Abyss condition?

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: *sigh* Yes, she got exposed to Abyssal energy as a young child... Then her birth parents abandoned her. It's lucky those wild qucusaurs found her when they did, or she wouldn't have made it. They took her under their wing and raised her as one of their own.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: Eventually, some riders out on patrol spotted her, and brought her back to the tribe... But she was practically feral at that point!

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: The moment you took your eyes off her, she'd be getting herself into a fight. Or she'd run away to be with the saurians. She seemed to prefer them to her own kind... She might as well have been a saurian in human form!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That must be the aloof period she mentioned, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like there was more going on than just being aloof...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: We later discovered that her exposure to the Abyss had planted seeds of conflict in her heart. So, we started trying to bring it under control...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: But ultimately, she's the only one who can control it. Anyway, she's much more human these days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, uh... Don't worry about her, she seems pretty stable to Paimon. Uh, she's probably only avoiding the checkups because she thinks it'll stop you guys from worrying about her.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: ...Yes, I'm well aware of that. She knows she needs to be careful. If her condition ever took a turn for the worse, she wouldn't be brushing it aside like this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then what's there to worry about?

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: It's just, every checkup she's been to, they find new cuts and bruises. Nothing to do with the Abyss, of course, oh no — that's all fine. The problem with her is, she's her own worst enemy!

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: She's been living dangerously again, I'm sure of it! That's why she's avoiding the checkups, she wants to hide it from us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... Yeah... Paimon can see her doing that....

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's not just Chasca, either. Chuychu's out there every day on the front lines too, following her big sister around... They're asking for trouble, both of them.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: Next time you see them, please tell them to be careful for me. Even if they don't want to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...In the past, she always had Chuychu to keep an eye on her. Now Chuychu's gone, and I just... I don't want to lose another daughter.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: Chasca's been increasingly reckless since Chuychu passed. It's like she's trying to make up for it somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: Next time you see her, please tell her to be careful for me. Even if she doesn't want to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: If she doesn't want to do these checkups anymore, that's fine. I just want her to stop putting herself in harm's way.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cusco rambles on about Chasca and Chuychu.\nYou patiently listen until the bitter end...

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Chasca! I summoned a qucusaur! They do still respond to me after all!

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: ...Although unfortunately, someone else summoned it away again before I had a chance to go for a flight...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Oh really? That is unfortunate... But if you can do it once, you can do it again. Keep at it, and you'll pass the trial eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: You're right! You know, I almost thought about giving up, but I'm glad I didn't.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Chasca! How's Coyllur doing?

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Huh? Who are you? And how do you know my name...?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: #Ahem, these are, uh... my friends. {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You came up in conversation the other day, because... I was telling them about up-and-coming warriors in our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, huh? So that's you? ...Uh, what do you mean up-and-coming? *sigh* I'm closer to being wingless than I am to passing the trial...

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Anyway... We haven't met before, have we? You look so familiar somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: #Hmm... Maybe you saw {M#him}{F#her} in the stadium? Or anywhere, really. {M#He}{F#She}'s been all over Natlan lately, so it's not surprising that you've seen {M#him}{F#her} around.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: ...If you say so...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Yeah, that must be it.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Coyllur! Chasca!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Here you are. I've been looking everywhere for you two.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Oh, Elder Allpa! What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: I thought I should tell you myself... We're going to redo the flying trials.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Redo them? How come? This is so unexpected... and I can't believe you came out here just to tell us that in person...

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: It's embarrassing to admit, but... due to time constraints, we didn't do a proper inspection of the arena before the last round of trials began. Then we started to notice many candidates performing worse than expected...

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: So we redid the inspection afterwards, and found a number of issues which likely impacted candidate performance.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: This was entirely our mistake, and I apologize unreservedly. I know it doesn't make up for it, but I thought bringing you this message in person was the least I could do.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Oh, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: #Chasca, these people you're with... Are they {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You've heard of us?

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: I have indeed. Gathering intel is an essential part of being a warrior — plus, you've already made quite a name for yourself in Natlan. Actually, I've been meaning to invite you to enjoy our tribe's hospitality for some time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hospitality? Ooh! That includes food, right?

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Of course it does. If you'll let us host you, you'll be treated quite lavishly. Mighty warriors are highly revered in our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Besides, we still owe you for your help during the war. Without you, we would have suffered far worse at the hands of the Abyss... So I'd like the chance to show you our gratitude, on behalf of the whole tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mighty warriors, plural? So Paimon counts, too...? Hehe, Paimon's starting to like you a lot!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: That should go without saying. Your flying skills are the envy of our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's a good point...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Flower-Feather Clan seems like a really nice bunch of people! We definitely need to take her up on this offer!

choices.text: Last time was just a... flying visit...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Well, I'd love to stay, but I'm afraid I still have to inform the other candidates about the retrials. With our younger generation's future on the line, there's no time to lose.

response.speaker: Coyllur
response.text: Wait, Elder Allpa! ...Lemme help. The sooner everyone gets the news, the better.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Very well... In that case, Chasca, could I leave you to entertain our guests?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Sure thing.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Okay, let's meet by the obsidian totem pole later. Coyllur, let's get going.

response.speaker: Coyllur
response.text: Okay!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Allpa and Coyllur fly away, riding a qucusaur....

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Alright, they're out of earshot. I'm just gonna come out and ask:

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...That qucusaur who responded to Coyllur's call — that was your doing, wasn't it?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I grew up with these creatures. I could tell something was off the second I saw it.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #{M#His}{F#Her} whole demeanor seemed less like a qucusaur and more like... well, you. So I figure you must have been pulling the strings somehow.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can't believe you saw through it...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #{M#He}{F#She} looked very flustered when Coyllur asked for a ride. So I whistled to give {M#him}{F#her} a chance to escape.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...And judging by the look on your face, that was a welcome intervention, huh?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: It's alright, if you'd rather your hidden talents remain hidden, I respect that. I won't press you for answers, and I'll keep my speculations to myself.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: You're the kind of person I'd still trust even if you had superpowers. I know you'd use them for good.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Technically, I deceived Coyllur... Does that count as "for good"?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I think the ends justify the means in this case. She just lacked confidence, and you helped her resolve her internal conflict.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: If you hadn't intervened, I likely would have gotten my "mom" to help out instead... Although, having said that, there's a small chance she might've recognized her and seen through the whole thing... that would've done more harm than good...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, luckily no harm was done in the end.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Yeah. Anyway, if you're free now, how about I give you that tour I promised?

choices.text: We never got to check the place out properly.

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: Hmph! Hah!

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: Hyah!

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: Ready? I'm gonna get you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh... are they fighting? Should we try and break them up?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: They're fine, just doing their daily combat training.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Combat training? A little young for that, aren't they?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Not to us, we're a tribe of warriors. In ancient times, we were the most elite troops in the nation, responsible for patrolling and defending all of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: And even though times have changed, we've kept our martial spirit alive.

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: Hey, is that Chasca?

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: Chasca, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: Can you come train with us?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: #Now's not a good time, I'm afraid. I'm showing {NICKNAME} and Paimon around. Maybe next time.

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon...? Wait! You mean that legendary warrior, and legendary flying expert?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Legendary? Uh, yep! That's us, alright!

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy
dialogues.text: Awesome... It's so cool that you can fly without having to ride a qucusaur. Even Chasca can only do that for short distances!

dialogues.speaker: Capac
dialogues.text: #Um, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}! Can you teach me some cool sword tricks?

dialogues.speaker: Yatlan
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}! My family's shop makes the best Volcano Cake, you gotta try it!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Ahem! Let's behave ourselves, everyone. These people are here as our guests. They're going to meet Elder Allpa in a few minutes, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Kotimy, instead of being jealous of other people's talents, why not work on developing your own?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Capac, there's no point trying any "cool sword tricks" until you've mastered the basics. Have you done all your sword drills today?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: And Yatlan... Easy does it, okay? Not every conversation has to turn into you plugging the family business.

dialogues.speaker: Kotimy & Yatlan & Capac
dialogues.text: Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Chasca's mini-lecture calms the children down, and they stop crowding you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Sorry about those kids, they just got overexcited when they heard your name. Hope it didn't bother you too much.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: This is a Volcano Cake that Yatlan forced into my hands. She said to think of it as an apology gift.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Whoa... it smells amazing! {NICKNAME}, you want some?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: That's good. Yatlan will be thrilled.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, Chasca, those kids really adore you! You're way better with them than Paimon expected. Paimon figured you'd be more... um... aloof, maybe?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Aloof, huh? Well, to be fair, there was a period when I was like that. Around the time when I first joined the tribe.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...But it's a terrible attitude to have as a peacemaker. It tends to turn situations that could've had a peaceful resolution into a stalemate that can only be resolved by force...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Resolved by force" meaning, beating both parties into submission?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Yep, exactly. As long as other options are available, I try to avoid that at all costs.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Someone once told me that peace imposed by force will crumble in a matter of days, but peace achieved through genuine dialogue actually benefits both sides.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Even if sometimes, the parties are only willing to negotiate because they're both armed to the teeth.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true...

response.speaker: Yatlan
response.text: Hey, Chasca!

response.speaker: Kotimy
response.text: Uncle Cusco knows you're back, and he's coming to get you!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Hmm? Oh... Thanks.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, gotta dash. I'll meet you at the totem pole up ahead. You can't miss it, it sticks out like a sore thumb.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, are you running away!?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: First rule of conflict resolution: Grab the fan and run before the you-know-what hits.

response.speaker: Capac
response.text: Hehe, trust Chasca to make even running away sound cool!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Sorry about this... Just stall him for me, okay? I'll explain everything later.

talks.objective: Coordinate with Chasca by splitting up

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: ...Are you sure you don't want to reconsider, Pixica?

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: I appreciate it, Boss. But honestly, I'm pretty happy with my life nowadays...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Pixica, they're redoing the flying trials... Huh? Mutota?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Ah, did Allpa send you? I was just telling Pixica the news, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: The way things are in the tribe these days... I mean, you don't need me to tell you. This here is no future for a seasoned warrior like you.

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: Come on, Boss, do you have any idea how long it's been? I've been Wingless for years now. I'm not cut out for that anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: Of course I'll do my part if we ever need to defend the tribe, but there's really no point in me trying out for the flying squad now.

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: I've already made my peace with it. Not everyone has what it takes to return to the sky after going Wingless... Elder Allpa's perseverance is something else.

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: And like... it's okay if I'm not destined for greatness. I might not have the qucusaurs' approval, but with my hot air balloons, I can still reach the skies...

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: Handling these balloons every day, seeing how the customers react, the looks on their faces... That's enough for me.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Finding something you love doing can be just as hard as passing the flying trial. It's worth holding onto.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fair enough... It's your choice, I won't force you.

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: Oh, by the way, you should try taking a balloon ride if you've got the time! Once you've been up there for yourself, you'll see why I love it so much!

choices.text: I'm a little busy at the moment.

response.speaker: Pixica
response.text: No problem! If you ever wanna give it a try, you know where to find me!

talks.objective: Go to the Obsidian Totem Pole

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hey, Zhunan. Gazing out at Ochkanatlan again, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: ...Chasca? What are you doing here, is something up?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The flying squad is hosting retrials again soon. Wanna give it another try?

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: Heh, maybe you're forgetting the definition of "Wingless." I've failed so many times already that I've decided to call it quits for good. I'm done.

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: Elder Allpa always goes out of her way to come and tell me when a new trial is coming up, and it's nice of her to think of me... but nothing's gonna change. I'm not going to suddenly pass just because they're holding another trial.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: They're making some big changes to the arena this time, so the flying experience should be smoother than before. Coyllur's gonna try again.

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: Ehh... No, forget it. If I was genuinely good enough to make the squad, the location shouldn't affect my chances.

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: A true Rider can fly confidently whatever the conditions... Like you and Elder Allpa.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: #Zhunan! They're redoing the— Huh? Chasca and {NICKNAME}? You're already here...

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Guess they already told you then, huh? Come on, let's go train together!

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: Um... I'm gonna sit this one out.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: What? Why? But you've always looked up to Elder Allpa...

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: She went wingless after her injury, and spent years drifting... but even she came back and made it in the end. If she can do it, why can't you?

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: I mean... I don't have that kind of perseverance. And besides, the last thing I wanna do is fail in front of her yet again...

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: *sigh* Come on, you know you don't need to worry about that... Alright, well... how about we just treat this as you being my mentor? Then will you train with me?

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: Um... I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Enough umming and ahhing! Let's just get up in the air and figure it out as we go!

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: Wait... Hold on! Slow down! I can't keep up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Well that's one way to do it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah... Zhunan unwittingly chose the hard way.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Heh, they've been best friends since they were kids. If anyone knows how to get Zhunan out of a rut, it's Coyllur.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You helped Coyllur deal with her internal conflict, and now, she's done the same for someone else... You know, people often talk about how one conflict leads to another, and so on.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But sometimes in life, things spiral in a good direction instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Chasca! Hey, Allpa!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry to keep you waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's alright. I bet my dad talked your heads off, huh? What did he say?

choices.text: That you used to run away from home nearly every other day...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Heh... I was sometimes a little impulsive back then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hah! That's putting it mildly!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Haha, the memories... It feels like it was only yesterday when we brought you back and had Cusco and his family take you in.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: ...Back then, no one imagined this feral child would grow up to be the strongest warrior of the Flower-Feather Clan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You were the one that brought Chasca back to the tribe?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: That's right. Elder Allpa was already a veteran rider by then. She spotted me while patrolling from the skies, and tracked down my qucusaur "mom."

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: "Mom" agreed that it was time I tried to re-enter human society... But I didn't know the first thing about being civilized. I clashed with everyone who had to deal with me.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: And look at you now, renowned throughout the land as a peacemaker... How time flies.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: When the day comes that I can't fly anymore, it'll be up to you to look after our tribe and our flying squad.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Mm... You know me, though. I'm not a natural commander, I'm better off as a lone wolf on the front line.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...So stick it out for at least a few more years, okay? Give Coyllur and the others time to come into their own.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Oh, stop...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait so...Isn't the leader just the strongest warrior in the tribe? At least, Paimon figured that's how your tribe would work.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Strength is certainly a core tenet in the Flower-Feather Clan. But strength means far more than martial prowess alone.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Heh, if it all came down to individual strength, I'd struggle to call myself a warrior, let alone a member of the flying squad. Any fighter in the tribe could take me down.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Really? I had you down as an elite warrior like Chasca...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Well, sorry to disappoint you. It was something I aspired to at one point, so much so that I went adventuring in the Cinder City, Ochkanatlan, to try and prove myself... But it was foolish of me. I wasn't ready.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: I came back empty handed and seriously injured. The fact that I survived was something, I suppose, but after that I never seriously considered myself a strong fighter.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: And yet, you still managed to become the leader of the flying squad, thanks to your experience and determination. All while battling those old injuries. Don't you think that's a display of strength in its own right?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: #Hah... Let's shelve this discussion for now. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, there are some simple refreshments on the table, please help yourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yesss! Paimon was waiting for that part!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Didn't you just gorge yourself on a whole bunch of Volcano Cakes?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, they were for the snack stomach! The refreshments stomach still has plenty of space!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew! Paimon is soooooo full...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Well, if you're enjoying our hospitality, feel free to stay with us as long as you like...

response.speaker: Warmi
response.text: Um... Elder Allpa! There's uh... Something's come up!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: ...Hmm?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: What happened? Is it serious? Shall I deal with it?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Um, it's... Some merchants showed up, not from our tribe. They said they're here to discuss some potential collaboration with us.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Why now, this is terrible timing... There are a few Wingless that we haven't managed to reach yet, and we still haven't inspected the retrial arena...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Let me handle the other errands while you meet with the merchants. You shouldn't be trying to do everything at your age.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should help too! Seems only fair after all that food we ate...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Huh... Well, much obliged. Chasca, the remaining Wingless are all people you know. Let's see... Pixica now manages the Floating Target Balloons...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Huascar's probably still addicted to "Eyes on the Feathered Prize," and Zhunan spends her days up on the flying platform, staring at the Cinder City... I'll leave you to tell them the news.

choices.text: We're not here for a free lunch.
Guess that comes with being an elder, huh?
And that nearly half of your peers got beaten up by you as a kid...

dialogues.speaker: Huascar
dialogues.text: A retrial? What's the point? I pretty much treat life like it's a game, haha... no qucusaur's ever going to approve of that, no matter how many times I try.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Huascar... I can assure you, qucusaurs wouldn't judge you for something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Huascar
dialogues.text: Well, they must be judging me for something. Maybe I lack fighting spirit, or just don't have the talent... Not everyone's a natural like you.

dialogues.speaker: Huascar
dialogues.text: Don't waste your time on me. You'll have better luck with the ones who still have their heads in the clouds.

dialogues.speaker: Huascar
dialogues.text: In the meantime... Hehe, I think I'm gonna treat myself to a few more games of "Eyes on the Feathered Prize"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeesh. There's Wingless, then there's being a total lost cause...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: He used to be a fierce warrior, actually. But fighting spirit alone won't win you the qucusaurs' approval.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are all qucusaurs so strict? The ones in Floating Target Balloons and Eyes on the Feathered Prize seem pretty chilled out.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's one thing to hang out and have fun, but quite another to take to the skies with a human life on your back.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Giving a ride to someone who's unqualified endangers not only the Rider, but also the qucusaur themselves. If the Rider makes a mistake, they both suffer the consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So we have a mutual understanding with the qucusaurs: if someone isn't up to standard, we have to reject them... even if it means breaking their hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm sorry, I didn't mean to keep you so long... I don't get to talk about my daughters much, and once I got going, I lost track of time.

dialogues.speaker: Cusco
dialogues.text: I should be getting back to work now, so... Ah, Chasca. Help me talk some sense into her, won't you?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: I didn't realize Chasca was out delivering the news... Looks like Allpa's finally learning how to delegate.

dialogues.speaker: Huascar
dialogues.text: Tsk... Next time! I'll definitely hit the jackpot next time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's that sound? Seems like it's coming from that bridge.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think Coyllur's feeling better now? Let's go back to that bridge and check!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, where did the time go? We should meet back up with Chasca before it gets any later. To get to the totem pole, we need to head north, right?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I can see where Pixica's coming from. The view from up high really is spectacular. I don't usually notice, because I tend to just zoom along without taking in the scenery...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Nice one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've notified all the Wingless on the list now, right? Where to next?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The trial arena. It's not far from the tribe.
